title: QuickSmith runflow conductor for on-demand admin utilities
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build QuickSmith, a lightweight runflow conductor that converts templated admin utilities into event-driven tasks. The conductor enables safe, idempotent execution of short-form runbooks triggered from multiple sources (Console, Slack, alert rules), emits structured telemetry for audit and quality checks, and provides a dry-run + sandbox mode for first-line support. This work ties into the Ops Toolkit Revamp initiative to reduce mean time to repair and standardize admin primitives across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Adminlets can be instantiated from a template and executed as an idempotent Task with a run_id
Triggers supported: console button, Slack slash command, webhook from SLO monitor
All executions emit structured telemetry to the Runflow Grafana dashboard with tokenized request IDs
Dry-run mode simulates execution and returns a diff of intended actions without mutating state
RBAC gating honors team roles and logs approval events for audit
architecture_notes: Runflow controller implemented as a small stateless service that materializes templates into Temporal workflows
Decision: use Temporal for short workflows to get built-in retries, signal support, and visibility
Execution paths: synchronous quick paths (<3s) route to an immediate worker; long-running or risky tasks are queued and require explicit approval
Sandbox mode runs against a namespaced test cluster to validate steps end-to-end before production rollout
We will emit lineage events to the existing ops-telemetry topic for downstream QC and billing attribution
tradeoffs_and_risks: Synchronous execution reduces latency but increases blast radius; risk mitigated with step-level timeouts and circuit breakers
Using Temporal adds an operational dependency but simplifies replay and long-running approvals compared to ad-hoc queues
Template expressiveness vs safety: limiting templates to a safe DSL reduces flexibility but prevents unsafe shell commands
Telemetry volume growth — need sampling strategy for low-severity adminlets
implementation_steps: Design runlet DSL and safety whitelist (confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/QuickSmith+DSL)
Prototype Temporal worker and sample adminlet templates (github.com/redwood-inference/ops-toolkit/pull/2345)
Integrate Slack slash command + OAuth verification (PR #2378)
Add dry-run and sandbox wiring with mock connectors (drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QuickSmithSandbox)
Create runflow Grafana dashboard and alerting for failed adminlet runs (grafana.redwood.com/d/ops/runflow-overview)
Security review and RBAC policy mapping with Security team
